newsitem.title: CANADA: Safeway, striking Canada workers to resume talks.
newsitem.headline: Safeway, striking Canada workers to resume talks.

text.p: Grocery chain Canada Safeway Ltd and unions representing 10,000 of its employees in the western province of Alberta were slated to meet with a mediator on Saturday in hopes of ending an often-heated six-week-old strike.

The company was viewing the move back to the bargaining table as the first positive development since employees of 73 Alberta stores walked off the job on March 26, Canada Safeway spokeswoman Toby Oswald said.

Canada Safeway, a unit of Pleasanton, Calif.-based Safeway Inc. and Alberta's largest grocery chain, said it gave its position on several issues to its striking unions and they were reviewing the material.
The positions included some changes from a "final offer" handed the employees just before talks broke off and the strike began, Oswald said.
She said it was yet known whether the unions, which include the United Food and Commercial Workers, and company officials would meet face to face on Saturday or just through the mediator.
Workers have been without a contract since March 1996.

The company's final offer included a 50-cent-per-hour wage increase and a C$1,000 payment for full-time workers if the deal was ratified. The five-year deal would also give full-time and senior part-time employees pay hikes of 30 cents an hour in 1998 and 40 cents in 2000.
Unions previously demanded the company fully restore C$2-an-hour wage rollbacks employees took in 1993.
The chain's stores have been run during the strike by management and replacement workers. But sales have dropped off as many customers avoided crossing picket lines, competitors have said.
Toronto-based Loblaw Cos Ltd. said last week that sales at its Real Canadian Superstore chain in Alberta had soared 30 percent since the Canada Safeway strike began.
